question: With every switch on the ELEC panel in AUTO (no lights), what is the only manual input normally needed?

options.text: Selecting AC ESS FEED to ALTN
Pressing EXT PWR to connect ground power

explanation: The electrical system is automatic for normal operation; connecting ground power is the one routine action.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Which sources do GEN 1 and GEN 2 have priority over when they are operating?

options.text: Both the APU generator and external power
Neither; the APU generator has top priority

explanation: Engine generators come first, then external power, then the APU generator.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: With the EXT PWR pushbutton ON, which source has priority between external power and the APU generator?
explanation: External power has priority over the APU generator; the engine generators have priority over both.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Can a single engine generator supply the entire electrical network?

options.text: No, it can supply only its own side
Yes, one engine generator can supply the whole network
Only with the galleys switched off manually

explanation: Each generator is sized for the whole aircraft; the bus ties connect it to the other side. Galley loads are shed in this case.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What is the normal voltage range shown on the BAT 1 and BAT 2 indicators?
explanation: The battery voltage indicators sit above the BAT pushbuttons; normal is 25–31 V.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What do the BAT 1 and BAT 2 pushbuttons control?
explanation: In AUTO each charge limiter connects or disconnects its battery from the DC BAT BUS automatically.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: In AUTO, the batteries are connected to the DC BAT BUS during which phase involving the APU?

options.text: While the APU is starting (MASTER SW ON and APU speed below 95 %)
While the APU is shutting down
While the APU bleed is in use
Whenever the APU generator is on line

explanation: The batteries help power the APU start and are disconnected again once it is up to speed.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Below what battery voltage does the charge limiter connect a battery to charge it?
explanation: A battery below 26.5 V is connected to the DC BAT BUS so it can be charged.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: With AC BUS 1 and 2 lost, below what speed are the batteries connected to the DC BAT BUS because the emergency generator is not supplying?
explanation: Below 100 kt the RAT cannot drive the emergency generator, so the batteries take over.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: With no AC BUS 1 or 2 and no emergency generator, what does battery 1 supply?

options.text: The AC STAT INV BUS, and the AC ESS BUS through the static inverter above 50 kt

explanation: Battery 1 drives the static inverter; battery 2 supplies the DC ESS BUS.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: With no AC BUS 1 or 2 and no emergency generator, what does battery 2 supply?
explanation: Battery 2 feeds DC essential; battery 1 feeds the static inverter side.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What happens when a BAT pushbutton is selected OFF?

options.text: The battery line contactor opens; the hot buses stay supplied
The battery is disconnected from the hot bus too
The battery is discharged into the DC BAT BUS
The battery's FAULT light comes on

explanation: OFF opens the line contactor (white OFF light when the DC BAT BUS is supplied), but the hot buses remain connected to the battery.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What causes a BAT FAULT light?

options.text: The battery charging current is outside limits, and the battery contactor opens
The battery has been off for more than 2 minutes

explanation: An abnormal charging current is a sign of a battery problem, so the battery is isolated.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: When does the green EXT PWR AVAIL light come on?

options.text: When external power is supplying the aircraft
When external power is plugged in and its parameters are normal
Whenever the aircraft is on the ground

explanation: AVAIL means ground power is ready; pressing the button then connects it and shows a white ON light.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Does the EXT PWR ON light go out when the engine generators take over the network?

options.text: No, the ON light stays on even when the engine generators supply the aircraft

explanation: The engine generators have priority, but the ON light remains until the crew deselects external power.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: When does a generator's line contactor close with the GEN pushbutton ON?

options.text: As soon as the engine starts
Only after the crew presses it a second time
Only when the APU generator is off
When the generator's electrical parameters are normal

explanation: The generator control unit checks voltage and frequency before connecting the generator to its bus.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What does selecting a GEN pushbutton OFF do?

options.text: Disconnects the IDG from the engine
Opens the line contactor, de-energises the generator and resets the fault circuit

explanation: GEN OFF is reversible, unlike the IDG disconnect.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What causes the GEN FAULT light?

options.text: The generator control unit tripping the generator, or the line contactor opening with the pushbutton not OFF

explanation: FAULT shows a protection trip or an unexpected open contactor.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Besides normal parameters, what condition must be met for the APU generator line contactor to close?

options.text: Both engine generators must be on line
The APU bleed must be off
The external power line contactor must be open

explanation: Because external power has priority, the APU generator connects only when external power is not supplying.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: When is the APU GEN FAULT light inhibited?

options.text: Whenever the aircraft is in flight
When APU speed is too low, or when external power or an engine generator is providing power
Whenever the APU bleed is on

explanation: In these cases an unconnected APU generator is normal, not a fault.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What does the BUS TIE pushbutton in AUTO do?

options.text: Keeps both bus tie contactors permanently closed
Opens or closes the bus tie contactors automatically to keep both AC BUS 1 and AC BUS 2 supplied
Connects the AC ESS BUS to AC BUS 2
Connects the batteries to the AC buses

explanation: The contactors close as needed so a single source can feed both sides.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: When are both bus tie contactors closed?

options.text: Only when both engine generators run
Never; only one can close at a time
In single-engine generator operation, or when the APU generator or external power supplies the network

explanation: With a single source, both sides must be tied to it.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What happens when the BUS TIE pushbutton is selected OFF?

options.text: Both bus tie contactors open, so each AC bus is supplied only by its own engine generator
Both AC buses are connected to the APU generator
The AC ESS BUS is shed
The batteries supply the AC buses

explanation: OFF isolates the two sides from each other.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: From which bus is the AC ESS BUS normally supplied?
explanation: AC ESS FEED in NORMAL supplies the AC ESS BUS from AC BUS 1; ALTN takes it from AC BUS 2.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: If the normal AC ESS feed fails, what happens without crew action?

options.text: The static inverter takes over after 30 seconds
The AC ESS BUS is automatically supplied from AC BUS 2 after 5 seconds

explanation: The automatic transfer happens regardless of the AC ESS FEED pushbutton position.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What does the AC ESS FEED FAULT light indicate?

options.text: The AC ESS BUS is not electrically supplied

explanation: FAULT, with an ECAM caution, means the essential AC bus itself has no power.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: In case of total loss of the main generators, what supplies the AC ESS BUS?

options.text: The emergency generator if available, otherwise the static inverter

explanation: The essential bus is kept alive first by the RAT-driven emergency generator, then by the batteries through the static inverter.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What does pressing a guarded IDG pushbutton do?

options.text: It disconnects the IDG from its drive shaft
It switches the generator off line only
It resets the IDG after an overheat
It tests the IDG oil pressure

explanation: The switches are spring-loaded out; pressing disconnects the drive mechanically.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Who can reconnect a disconnected IDG?

options.text: The crew, by pressing the IDG pushbutton again
The crew, by cycling the GEN pushbutton

explanation: The disconnection cannot be reversed from the cockpit.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Above what IDG oil outlet temperature does the IDG FAULT light come on?
explanation: An IDG oil overheat above 185 °C, or low IDG oil pressure, gives the FAULT light.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: When is the IDG low oil pressure fault inhibited?

options.text: At low engine speed, with N2 below 14 %

explanation: A stopped or slow engine naturally has low IDG oil pressure, so the alert is inhibited.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: With GALY & CAB in AUTO, when is the cabin power shed?

options.text: Whenever the APU generator is supplying
When only one generator is operating

explanation: One generator cannot comfortably carry the galleys; with the APU generator or external power all galleys are available.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: When does the GALY & CAB FAULT light come on?

options.text: When the cabin power is shed
When any generator's load exceeds 100 % of its rated output
When the commercial pushbutton is off

explanation: The FAULT warns the crew that cabin loads are overloading the generators.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Which of these is switched off by the COMMERCIAL pushbutton?
explanation: COMMERCIAL covers cabin and cargo lights, water and toilet, drain mast ice protection, galley, entertainment and cargo loading.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Which condition, together with the loss of AC BUS 1 and AC BUS 2, makes the RAT extend automatically?
explanation: With both main AC buses lost above 100 kt, the RAT extends and the Blue system drives the emergency generator.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: When is the emergency generator connected to the network after an automatic RAT extension?

options.text: As soon as its electrical parameters are within tolerance
When the crew presses MAN ON

explanation: The generator is brought on line once its voltage and frequency are correct.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: After a manual RAT extension with MAN ON, when is the emergency generator coupled?

options.text: 3 seconds after the RAT is supplying the emergency generator

explanation: MAN ON selects manual RAT extension; coupling follows 3 s after the RAT drives the generator.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: When does the red FAULT light on the EMER ELEC PWR panel come on?

options.text: When the static inverter is in use
When the emergency generator is not supplying power while AC BUS 1 and AC BUS 2 are unpowered

explanation: It is red because the aircraft is then running on batteries alone.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: During the EMER GEN TEST on the ground with normal AC buses, which buses are NOT powered by the emergency generator?

options.text: The AC ESS SHED and DC ESS SHED buses

explanation: The test connects AC ESS and DC ESS to the emergency generator, driven by the Blue electric pump; the shed buses lose power.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What happens when GEN 1 LINE is selected OFF?

options.text: GEN 1 shuts down and the IDG disconnects
GEN 1's line contactor opens; GEN 1 keeps running and supplies one fuel pump in each wing directly

explanation: AC BUS 1 is then supplied from GEN 2 through the bus ties.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What does the amber SMOKE light on the GEN 1 LINE pushbutton indicate?

options.text: Smoke in the avionics ventilation duct

explanation: GEN 1 LINE is part of the smoke drill used to isolate an electrical smoke source.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: On the ECAM ELEC page, when is the battery current shown in amber?

options.text: When it is charging at more than 1 A
When the battery is discharging at more than 5 A
When it is above 30 A in either direction
Whenever the battery contactor is closed

explanation: A large discharge means the battery is carrying loads it should not.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: On the ELEC page, what does an amber arrow pointing away from the battery mean?

options.text: The contactor is closed and the battery is discharging at more than 1 A

explanation: A green arrow is charging above 1 A; amber is discharging above 1 A; no line is an open contactor.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: When is the DC BAT voltage shown in amber on the ELEC page?
explanation: DC BAT below 25 V is amber.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What does an amber SHED next to a bus on the ELEC page mean?

options.text: The AC or DC ESS SHED bus is in shed mode
The bus is supplied by the APU

explanation: Shedding removes the less essential loads from the essential network.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: When is a TR's current shown in amber on the ELEC page?
explanation: A TR delivering almost no current is likely not supplying its bus.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Outside what voltage range is a generator's voltage shown in amber?
explanation: Generator voltage is amber below 110 V or above 120 V.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Outside what frequency range is a generator's frequency shown in amber?
explanation: Frequency is amber below 390 Hz or above 410 Hz.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: When is a generator load shown in amber on the ELEC page?
explanation: Over 100 % load is beyond the rated output.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: On the ELEC page, what does amber APU GEN with a white OFF show?

options.text: The APU master switch is ON but the APU GEN pushbutton is off

explanation: The APU is running but its generator has been deselected.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Between what IDG oil outlet temperatures does the indication pulse on the ELEC page?
explanation: It pulses above 147 °C as an advisory and turns amber above 180 °C.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What does an amber DISC under the IDG legend on the ELEC page mean?

options.text: The IDG is disabled by the crew's GEN OFF

explanation: LO PR would mean low IDG oil pressure; DISC means the drive has been disconnected.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.
